title: Roast Chicken with Pan Gravy & Potatoes
subtitle: a golden butter-rubbed whole chicken roasted over potatoes, carrots and onion, with gravy from the pan
imageAlt: A golden roast chicken with roast potatoes and carrots and a jug of gravy on a white platter with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for two, plus plenty for sandwiches and soup

beforeYouStart.text: A frozen whole chicken needs about 2 days in the fridge to thaw.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before roasting and pat it very dry for crisp skin.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the chicken dry. Mash the butter with the garlic powder, paprika, dried thyme, salt and pepper; rub some under the breast skin and the rest all over. Put the lemon halves inside.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with the oil and salt in a roasting pan or large metal pan. Set the chicken on top, breast side up.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 190°C (375°F) and roast 55–65 minutes more, until the thickest part of the thigh reads 82°C (180°F) and the juices run clear.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Lift the chicken onto a board and tent with foil for 15 minutes. Move the vegetables to a baking sheet and return them to the oven to crisp.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Pour the pan juices into a cup and spoon 2 tbsp of the fat back into the pan. Set it over medium, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and the juices (not the rest of the fat), scraping up the brown bits. Simmer 4–5 minutes until thick; season to taste.

steps.title: Carve
steps.text: Carve the legs, then the breasts, and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

fixIt.fix: Dry the chicken well and don't cover it in the oven; a few minutes at 220°C (425°F) at the end helps.
Keep roasting until the thigh reads 82°C (180°F); tent the breast loosely with foil so it doesn't dry out.
Simmer a few minutes longer, or whisk in 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp cold water.

saleTip: Whole chickens are often about $6.60/kg at No Frills, cheaper per kilo than parts; the bones make next week's soup.
swap: Russet potatoes work too; cut them a little bigger.
leftovers: Pull the meat for sandwiches, pot pie or chicken noodle soup, and simmer the carcass for broth.
doneness: Whole chicken at 82°C (180°F) in the thickest part of the thigh, not touching bone (Health Canada, whole poultry).
source: Based on tested roast chicken methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): butter-rubbed bird started at 220°C then roasted at 190°C over root vegetables, rested, with a flour-thickened pan gravy.
gear: Roasting pan or large metal pan
prepAhead: Season the chicken the night before and leave it uncovered in the fridge for extra-crisp skin.
Cut the vegetables up to 1 day ahead; keep the potatoes covered in water.
reheat: Sliced chicken covered with a splash of broth at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Butter, garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper; no lemon or dried thyme.

stepNotes.0: Basic: skip the dried thyme and lemon.

fancy.note: A whole head of roasted garlic and a splash of cream in the gravy.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: tuck the halved garlic head, cut side up, among the vegetables.

addSteps.title: Fancy gravy
addSteps.text: Squeeze 4 roasted garlic cloves into the gravy and whisk in the cream; simmer 1 minute. Serve the rest of the garlic for spreading.

plating: Whole bird on a platter on the vegetables, carved at the table.
Roasted garlic halves on the platter.

why.0-1: Butter under the skin bastes the breast from the inside.
why.1-0: The potatoes roast in the chicken drippings, the best part of the pan.
why.2-0: Flour cooked in the fat gives a smooth gravy with no lumps.

funFact: A rested bird loses far less juice on the board than one carved straight from the oven, so the 15 minutes are worth it.

keeps.note: freeze the meat off the bone, in gravy or broth

pairs: the next day, with the leftover chicken
